blocks.text: Most verbs are **twins**: an **imperfective** (the action itself — going on, repeated, or just named) and a **perfective** (one action completed, a result).

head: Imperfective (писа́ть)
Perfective (написа́ть)
rows: писа́л — I wrote, was writing, used to write
blocks.caption: The five tenses of a twin verb

blocks.text: A perfective verb has **no present**: its present-type forms are the future. Never **буду** + perfective.

Where English uses the present after *when, as soon as, if* about the future, Russian uses the **future**: **Когда́ я ко́нчу** работу, я позвоню. *When I finish…* **Е́сли бу́дет** дождь, мы не пойдём. *If it rains…*

exercises.why: Finished, then the next action → perfective.

exercises.q: *Если завтра ___ хорошая погода, мы поедем за город.*
Когда я ___ эту книгу, я дам её тебе. (прочитать — I finish reading)
Что ты ___ ? (купить — what will you buy?)
